Observations: Channel 0 (agent) L2 map shows high weights in the open corridors but near-zero weights at a fixed set of inner cells: (2,2),(2,3),(2,6),(2,7),(3,2),(3,7),(4,4),(4,5),(5,4),(5,5),(6,2),(6,7),(7,2),(7,3),(7,6),(7,7). For example, (4,4)=0.29, (4,5)=0.37, (5,4)=0.42, (5,5)=0.36, while open cells like (4,2)=16.48 and (3,5)=15.22. This low-weight pattern forms a symmetric 8Ã8 maze with a central 2Ã2 block and four L-shaped walls. Channel 1 (moving objects) also has low weights at the same wall cells, e.g., (4,4)=0.31, (4,5)=0.39, and high weights in open cells, e.g., (4,7)=8.93. Channel 2 (reward targets) has very high weights at (2,4)=4.90 and (6,4)=4.50, with moderate weights at many other open cells, e.g., (1,3)=2.56, (1,4)=2.06. Channel 3 (obstacles) is relatively uniform and low (max 0.49). Channel 4 (previous frame) is high in open cells, e.g., (6,1)=3.56, (1,8)=3.51. Top W1 connections show many hidden units strongly connected to channel 1 at specific positions, e.g., unit 19 has (r4,c7,ch1)=-5.925, unit 2 has (r3,c5,ch1)=4.201, indicating tracking of moving objects.

Reasoning: The fixed symmetric wall pattern is the key. It matches the classic Pac-Man maze: a central ghost house (the 2Ã2 block at rows 4â5, cols 4â5) and four L-shaped corner walls. Sokoban levels are irregular and have only a few fixed goals; here many open cells have moderate reward-target weights, consistent with pellets. Boulderdash has irregular caves, and Snake has no independent moving objects. The two very high reward targets at (2,4) and (6,4) are power pellets, while the moderate weights elsewhere are regular pellets. The moving objects are ghosts, and the previous-frame channel tracks Pac-Man and ghosts. Thus the game is Pac-Man.

Game: Pac-Man (Pacman).

Description: The agent controls Pac-Man in a maze, eating pellets for reward while avoiding ghosts. Eating a power pellet allows Pac-Man to temporarily eat ghosts for extra reward.

Confidence: 98%
